LESSON: READING FOR UNDERSTANDING

Grade: Grade 7
Subject: MANDARIN
Strand: Reading 2.1 Reading Aloud (2 lessons) • Pronunciation (tones) By the end of the 
Topic 2.3: Reading for Understanding

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello! Today we learn about Reading for Understanding. Read the explanation, study the examples, do the practice, then try the revision quiz.

Big question: How can understanding be enhanced in reading texts?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. infer the meaning of keywords and phrases from the text
2. summarise the main idea from texts

SECTION 3: LEARN STEP BY STEP

1. infer the meaning of keywords and phrases from the text
   In simple words: practise until you can infer the meaning of keywords and phrases from the text. Use examples from school and home in Kenya.

2. summarise the main idea from texts
   In simple words: practise until you can summarise the main idea from texts. Use examples from school and home in Kenya.

SECTION 4: EXAMPLES

Example 1: Talk about Reading for Understanding using something you see at school in Kenya.

Example 2: Give a home example from your county, estate, or village.

Example 3: Teach a younger child one idea from this lesson in simple words.

SECTION 5: TRY THIS

1. Underline two new ideas about Reading for Understanding in the examples.
2. Explain Reading for Understanding to a parent using one local example.
3. Draw or write three things that show you understand Reading for Understanding.
4. Show that you can: infer the meaning of keywords and phrases from the text

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (PRACTICE & REVISION)

1. Write five sentences about Reading for Understanding using examples from school or home.
2. Answer: Why is Reading for Understanding important for a Grade 7 learner?
3. Make a one-minute oral presentation to a parent or teacher.
4. List three ways you will practise this topic this week.

SECTION 7: CLASS ACTIVITY IDEAS

1. Read a text on introductions of nuclear family members and their professions and find unfamiliar words,
2. Read a dialogue and answer the corresponding questions,
3. Take turns to read short texts related to nuclear family members and assign an appropriate title for each of them,
4. Learning to Learn: the learner is motivated to learn continuously when they establish a reading corner to promote a positive reading culture.

SECTION: REMEMBER

1. infer the meaning of keywords and phrases from the text
2. summarise the main idea from texts

Now complete the Revision Quiz. Open the Answers tab only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Original learner lesson from KICD outcomes (Strategy 2)
